name: Baal-Hanan
title: King of Edom
summary: Baal-Hanan, son of Achbor, was one of the early kings who reigned in Edom before Israel had kings. He is mentioned in the genealogies in Genesis and 1 Chronicles as part of the list of Edomite kings, representing the political organization of Esau's descendants.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the List of Edomite Kings
keyEvents.description: Baal-Hanan, son of Achbor, became king in Edom after the death of Saul (an Edomite Saul, not Israel's Saul). He is listed as one of the kings who reigned in Edom before the kings of Israel.

keyEvents.title: The Line of Edomite Kings in Chronicles
keyEvents.description: Baal-Hanan is mentioned again in 1 Chronicles as part of the same list of Edomite rulers, confirming his historical role.

keyEvents.title: Successor to the Previous King
keyEvents.description: Baal-Hanan took the throne after the death of the preceding Edomite king, Saul from Rehoboth by the River, and continued the governance of Edom.

keyEvents.title: Succeeded by Hadar
keyEvents.description: When Baal-Hanan, son of Achbor, died, Hadar (also called Hadad) became king in his place. His wife was named Mehetabel, daughter of Matred.

keyEvents.title: Part of Esau's lineage
keyEvents.description: The king list where Baal-Hanan is mentioned is part of the broader account of Esau's descendants and their establishment in the land of Edom, showing God's fulfillment of the promise that Esau would also become a great nation.
